observed_anchors: The accepted-target V4 counterworld demonstrated two byte-distinct SQLite 3.53.4 builds with the same upstream sqlite_source_id can each be admitted when the caller supplies the matching manifest digest; caller-selected manifest identity is therefore self-consistency, not independent deployment authority.

V5 removes the caller-supplied manifest digest choice and instead requires /etc/frank-v0.1/sqlite-runtime-anchor-v1.json with root ownership, non-group/non-other-writable parent chain, symlink rejection, lstat/fstat inode continuity, and parent-to-child anchor digest continuity.

The accepted target is Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, runs the self-hosted lane as frankrunner uid 1000, has no /etc/frank-v0.1 directory or V5 anchor, and the V5 launcher fails closed before productive code with exit 78 when the anchor is absent.
The accepted-target runner has no passwordless sudo, so a positive root-owned anchor mechanism probe cannot be created by the current CI authority lane.
The initial V5 mechanism workflow represented this blocked positive probe as a successful workflow conclusion; that was evidence-semantics false-green rather than a runtime admission PASS.
Frank main concurrently integrated the V5 pre-guard PATH fence so caller-controlled PATH helpers are not executed before the Python V5 guard.
